subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: Should OpenClaw standardize framework-authenticated memory provenance plus retrieval authority controls in the shared memory-plugin contract, or keep source-trust policy as an optional plugin/MCP capability?
rationale: Current policy treats workspace memory as trusted operator state and current memory guidance is advisory; only maintainers can choose whether changing that model is a core security commitment, a default-memory-plugin responsibility, or an external extension concern.

options.title: Design a bounded shared memory contract
options.body: Define framework-owned origin, review, expiry, and influence fields plus the minimum retrieval/promotion hooks, then let the selected memory plugin enforce the policy.

options.title: Keep it extension-owned
options.body: Document the supported plugin/MCP route and require each memory implementation to own its trust semantics without changing the shared default contract.

options.title: Defer while retaining the provenance prerequisite
options.body: Advance the narrower source-attribution work first and revisit enforcement once its storage and retrieval contract is proven.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded shared memory contract
recommendation.body: Define framework-owned origin, review, expiry, and influence fields plus the minimum retrieval/promotion hooks, then let the selected memory plugin enforce the policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review already routed this exact cross-cutting memory/security design question through the current memory contract area.
